COBOL.fact: COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language; ) is a compiled English-like computer programming language designed for business use. COBOL is primarily used in business, finance, and administrative systems for companies and governments.

COBOL.question: It was created as part of a US _____ of Defense effort to create a portable programming language for data processing
COBOL.fact: It was created as part of a US Department of Defense effort to create a portable programming language for data processing. It was originally seen as a stopgap, but the Defense Department promptly pressured computer manufacturers to provide it, resulting in its widespread adoption.

COBOL.question: It was originally seen as a stopgap, but the _____ promptly pressured computer manufacturers to provide it, resulting in its widespread adoption
COBOL.fact: It was originally seen as a stopgap, but the Defense Department promptly pressured computer manufacturers to provide it, resulting in its widespread adoption.

COBOL.fact: The current standard is ISO/IEC 1989:2023.

COBOL.fact: A 1959 survey had found that in any data processing installation, the programming cost US$800,000 on average and that translating programs to run on new hardware would cost US$600,000. On 8 April 1959, Mary K. Hawes, a computer scientist at Burroughs Corporation, called a meeting of representatives from academia, computer users, and manufacturers at the University of Pennsylvania to organize a formal meeting on common business languages.

COBOL.subject: Computer & IT
COBOL.question: Representatives included _____ (inventor of the English-like data processing language FLOW-MATIC), Jean Sammet, and Saul Gorn
COBOL.fact: Representatives included Grace Hopper (inventor of the English-like data processing language FLOW-MATIC), Jean Sammet, and Saul Gorn.

COBOL.subject: Computer & IT
COBOL.question: The delegation impressed _____, director of the Data System Research Staff at the DoD, who thought that they "thoroughly understood" the DoD's problems
COBOL.fact: The delegation impressed Charles A. Phillips, director of the Data System Research Staff at the DoD, who thought that they "thoroughly understood" the DoD's problems.

COBOL.subject: Computer & IT
COBOL.question: It was attended by 41 people and was chaired by _____
COBOL.fact: Charles Phillips agreed to sponsor the meeting, and tasked the delegation with drafting the agenda. It was attended by 41 people and was chaired by Phillips.

COBOL.question: The Department of _____ was concerned about whether it could run the same data processing programs on different computers
COBOL.fact: The Department of Defense was concerned about whether it could run the same data processing programs on different computers.

COBOL.fact: The committee mainly examined the FLOW-MATIC, AIMACO, and COMTRAN programming languages. The FLOW-MATIC language was particularly influential because it had been implemented and because AIMACO was a derivative of it with only minor changes.

COBOL.fact: FLOW-MATIC's inventor, Grace Hopper, also served as a technical adviser to the committee. COBOL.fact: In 1980, Grace Hopper commented that "COBOL 60 is 95% FLOW-MATIC" and that COMTRAN had had an "extremely small" influence. Computer science.fact: == History == The earliest foundations of what would become computer science predate the invention of the modern digital computer. CPU cache.question: The _____ was Hardware cache of a central processing unit.
CPU cache.fact: A CPU cache is a hardware cache used by the central processing unit (CPU) of a computer to reduce the average cost (time or energy) to access data from the main memory.

CPU cache.subject: Computer & IT
CPU cache.question: Cache memory is typically implemented with static random-access memory (_____), which requires multiple transistors to store a single bit
CPU cache.fact: Cache memory is typically implemented with static random-access memory (SRAM), which requires multiple transistors to store a single bit. Some modern designs implement some or all of their cache using the physically smaller eDRAM, which is slower to use than SRAM but allows larger amounts of cache for any given amount of chip area.

CPU cache.subject: Computer & IT
CPU cache.question: Some modern designs implement some or all of their cache using the physically smaller eDRAM, which is slower to use than _____ but allows larger amounts of cache for any given amount of chip area

CPU cache.subject: Computer & IT
CPU cache.question: The memory device with that value, normally implemented in _____, holds that value in a very low-energy form that is not powerful enough to be read directly by the CPU
CPU cache.fact: The memory device with that value, normally implemented in DRAM, holds that value in a very low-energy form that is not powerful enough to be read directly by the CPU. By locating the memory physically closer to the CPU the time needed for the buses to settle is reduced, and by replacing the DRAM with SRAM, which hold the value in a form that does not require amplification to be read, the delay within the memory itself is eliminated.

CPU cache.subject: Computer & IT
CPU cache.question: A single TLB can be provided for access to both instructions and data, or a separate _____ TLB (ITLB) and data TLB (DTLB) can be provided
CPU cache.fact: Many modern desktop, server, and industrial CPUs have at least three independent levels of caches (L1, L2 and L3) and different types of caches: Translation lookaside buffer (TLB) Used to speed up virtual-to-physical address translation for both executable instructions and data. A single TLB can be provided for access to both instructions and data, or a separate Instruction TLB (ITLB) and data TLB (DTLB) can be provided.
